title: Cardiac Rehabilitation (Coronary Artery Disease, Post-MI, PCI and CABG)
lead: Exercise is medicine for the heart, but it must be prescribed with precision.
case: A 58-year-old man, 3 weeks after inferior MI treated with a stent. Ejection fraction preserved. On a beta-blocker. Resting HR 62, BP 126/78. No angina since. Goal: return to work as a schoolteacher.
working: Cardiac Rehabilitation (Coronary Artery Disease, Post-MI, PCI and CABG)
plan: Phase I to III as above. Long-term goal: at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week plus strength training [Ref – to verify].
qa: How will you set intensity? RPE 11 to 14, because the beta-blocker blunts HR response.
Why a longer warm-up? It reduces the risk of ischaemia and arrhythmia.
He develops chest tightness during cycling that eases with rest in 2 minutes. Action? Stop, monitor, document; inform the medical team; set the next intensity below this threshold.
What risk factors will you address? Smoking, BP, cholesterol, diabetes, weight, inactivity, stress.
Why does cardiac rehabilitation matter? It reduces mortality and readmission and improves quality of life.

redFlags.Finding: Chest pain at rest or not relieved by rest and GTN within minutes
redFlags.Immediate action: Stop; call emergency services; follow GTN and aspirin protocol as prescribed

redFlags.Finding: New palpitations with dizziness or collapse
redFlags.Immediate action: Stop; emergency response; begin CPR and use AED if unresponsive without normal breathing

redFlags.Finding: Sternal clicking, wound discharge, fever after CABG
Groin swelling or pain after femoral PCI

manualNotes: Traditional precautions restrict lifting and pushing for about 6 to 8 weeks. Many centres now use more individual, movement-based approaches ("Keep Your Move in the Tube": keep upper arm movements close to the body during loaded tasks) [Ref – to verify]. Follow the surgical team's protocol.

exercise.Prescription: 10 to 15 min of gradually increasing low-intensity activity (important to prevent ischaemia)
20 to 40 min; 3 to 5 days a week; intensity 40 to 70% HRR or RPE 11 to 14; keep HR at least about 10 beats below any ischaemic threshold [Ref – to verify]
Start after the early phase as cleared (later for sternotomy); 1 to 3 sets of 10 to 15 reps at RPE 11 to 13, major muscle groups, 2 to 3 days a week; avoid breath holding
Risk factors, medication, recognising symptoms, GTN use, diet, smoking, stress, return to work and driving

exerciseNotes: Use RPE when on beta-blockers. Circuit and interval formats are acceptable for suitable patients.
modalityNotes: Not applicable. Home monitoring devices (pedometers, heart rate monitors) support adherence.
pathway: Phase I to III as above. Long-term goal: at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week plus strength training [Ref – to verify].
